summary: 5 repair targets triaged: q1-q4 should be rewritten as question-only text, and q5 should be removed because test placement can be decided by project patterns during spec/test planning.

items.title: 1. q1 includes rationale and recommendation
items.rationale: The pending question is valid, but pending QA entries must not include the recommended answer or rationale in the question text.
items.evidence: draft.json qa[id=q1].question asks the metricsSummary default-output boundary and also embeds a recommendation and reason.

items.title: 2. q2 includes rationale and recommendation
items.rationale: The pending question is valid as a user-facing CLI contract decision, but the recommendation and rationale must be removed from the question text.
items.evidence: draft.json qa[id=q2].question asks the details option name and also embeds `--details` as the recommendation with a reason.

items.title: 3. q3 includes rationale and recommendation
items.rationale: The pending question is valid because request and mergeStrategy are user-visible output fields, but it must ask only the decision.
items.evidence: draft.json qa[id=q3].question asks whether request and mergeStrategy remain in default output and also embeds a split recommendation.

items.title: 4. q4 includes rationale and recommendation
items.rationale: The pending question is valid because recovery fields affect status consumers, but pending question text must not include the proposed answer.
items.evidence: draft.json qa[id=q4].question asks the reviewStop/gateStop default-output boundary and also embeds a recommendation to keep retryRecovery only.

items.title: 5. q5 asks internal implementation details and includes recommendation
items.rationale: The test strategy is already deferred to spec and can be resolved from existing project patterns, so this user question should be removed instead of rewritten.
items.evidence: draft.json decisionMap.deferredToSpec already says default/details contract, runId coverage, unknown option test, and help text updates will be defined in spec test strategy.
